Name: Shared Skills
Author: Fetterus
Description:
[size=5][b]Shared Skills[/b][/size]

Skill experience is shared between every player on the farm, wherever they are and whatever they are doing. If one player catches a fish, everyone gains the fishing experience.

Levels and professions stay individual: only raw experience is shared, so each player levels up on their own and picks their own professions.

Pairs well with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/49258]Shared Friendship[/url] — same rules, fully independent, use either or both.

[line]

[size=4][b]Features[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Every skill, in real time.[/b] Farming, Fishing, Foraging, Mining and Combat. Experience is shared the moment it is earned, no matter where on the map anyone is.[/*]
[*][b]Professions stay yours.[/b] You cross each level on your own and get your own profession menu that night. Two players can take opposite professions in the same skill.[/*]
[*][b]Offline farmhands keep up.[/b] Players who are not logged in still receive experience. Their progress is waiting for them when they come back.[/*]
[*][b]Catch-up for new players.[/b] Someone joining a farm that is already underway is brought up to speed once, when they connect. Works in both directions: a farmhand who joins ahead of everyone else raises the rest of the farm to their level.[/*]
[*][b]Install partway through a save.[/b] The same catch-up runs once when the host loads a save for the first time with the mod.[/*]
[*][b]Tune the rate.[/b] A global multiplier, a per-skill multiplier, and a per-skill on/off switch. With a multiplier above 1, everyone — the earner included — ends at exactly the multiplied amount. Optionally split the shared portion across the players online.[/*]
[*][b]Overflow for maxed skills (optional, off by default).[/b] XP landing on a skill that is already maxed can be redirected to your remaining skills instead of being lost. Once everything is at 10 it steps aside and Mastery flows as normal.[/*]
[*][b]Custom skills.[/b] Skills added by other mods through SpaceCore are shared too, each one toggleable on its own.[/*]
[*][b]The host's settings apply to everyone[/b] for the duration of a session. Your own config file is left alone and comes back when you leave.[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=4][b]Installation[/b][/size]

[list=1]
[*]Install [url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI[/url] 4.0.0 or later. Stardew Valley 1.6 or later is required.[/*]
[*]Unzip into your [b]Stardew Valley/Mods[/b] folder.[/*]
[*][b]Every player must install it.[/b] This is not optional. A player without the mod is warned in the chat box and simply does not take part in sharing; the rest of the farm keeps syncing between themselves.[/*]
[*]Run the game once to generate [b]config.json[/b].[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=4][b]Configuration[/b][/size]

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] is optional but recommended: it gives you all of this in game, with no file editing. Without it, edit [b]config.json[/b] by hand.

[code]
Setting                Default    What it does
---------------------  ---------  -----------------------------------------------
Enabled                true        Turn sharing off. Nobody loses progress.
GlobalXpMultiplier      1.0        Applied to every shared gain. Range 0.1 to 10.
PerSkillEnabled        all true    Per-skill on/off switch.
PerSkillMultiplier      all 1.0    Multiplied with the global multiplier.
DividePerPlayerCount    false      Split the shared portion across the players
                                    online. Your own vanilla gains are never
                                    reduced.
ShareMasteryXp          true        Keep sharing from maxed skills, which feeds
                                    Mastery.
OverflowMaxedSkillXp    false      Redirect XP landing on a maxed skill to your
                                    remaining skills instead of losing it.
CatchUpPolicy          SyncToMax  SyncToMax, SyncToHost, or FutureGainsOnly.
ShareSpaceCoreSkills    true        Share custom skills from other mods.
SpaceCoreSkillEnabled  {}          Per-custom-skill on/off switch.[/code]
While you are in someone else's session, the settings menu edits your own config rather than the host's. Your changes take effect when you leave.

The config menu will warn you when a multiplier below 1 (or splitting between players) is being cancelled out by the default SyncToMax catch-up policy — see the FAQ below for why.

[line]

[size=4][b]Console commands[/b][/size]

[code]
sharedskills_status  Experience per player and skill, plus which
                      players have the mod
sharedskills_sync    Host only. Force a catch-up now[/code]
If you ever report a problem, paste the output of [b]sharedskills_status[/b] with it — it answers most questions at a glance.

[line]

[size=4][b]Compatibility[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/1348]SpaceCore[/url] custom skills are supported[/b] and shared like any other skill, with a toggle per skill. Tested with Sword & Sorcery. (Overflow only redirects between the five vanilla skills.)[/*]
[*][b]Level-extending mods work.[/b] No experience table is hardcoded anywhere: the game's own level calculation decides what a level costs, and those mods change that calculation. Raising the cap past 10 needs no changes here. Only raw experience crosses the wire, never levels.[/*]
[*][b]Anything that grants experience through the game's normal path is shared[/b], whether that is vanilla, a quest mod, or a new skill.[/*]
[*]Works in split-screen and in networked co-op.[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=4][b]FAQ[/b][/size]

[b]Do we all get the same professions?[/b]
No, and that is the point. Only experience is shared. You cross each level yourself and get your own profession menu that night. Two players can pick opposite professions in the same skill.

[b]Someone joined late with nothing. Do they get caught up?[/b]
Yes, once, when they connect. They will get several profession menus in a row that first night, which is expected. Set CatchUpPolicy to FutureGainsOnly if you would rather they earn it from scratch.

[b]Does experience get multiplied by the number of players?[/b]
By default everyone receives the full amount, so a group levels faster than a solo player. Turning on DividePerPlayerCount splits the shared portion, which reduces the group's pace — but your own vanilla gains are never reduced, so the group still levels somewhat faster than a solo player would.

[b]Can I make the group slower than playing alone?[/b]
No. The floor is vanilla: this mod never subtracts, and your own actions always grant the full XP the game gives. Multipliers below 1 and splitting between players only shrink the shared portion. On top of that, with the default SyncToMax catch-up policy the morning pass raises everyone back to the highest total, so a reduction only delays the group by a day — for a reduction that sticks, also set CatchUpPolicy to FutureGainsOnly. The only way down to pure vanilla pace is turning the mod off.

[b]What happens to XP earned in a skill that is already maxed?[/b]
In vanilla, that XP is simply lost until every skill reaches 10 (then it feeds Mastery). With OverflowMaxedSkillXp turned on, it is redirected and split between your skills that are not maxed yet. Once everything is at 10 there is nothing left to redirect, so the option steps aside and Mastery flows exactly as vanilla. One quirk that comes with the territory: for a player already at total level 25+, natively earned XP in a maxed skill still grants Mastery AND overflows — you cannot have one without the other, because the game credits Mastery before this mod ever sees the gain.

[b]What if one player does not have the mod?[/b]
They are named in the chat box when they connect, and they do not take part. Everyone else keeps sharing normally. Nothing breaks.

[b]Can I uninstall it?[/b]
Yes. Delete the folder. Nothing is written to your save that the game does not already understand: this mod only ever grants experience through the game's own methods. Your levels and professions are ordinary save data and stay exactly as they are.

[b]What about Luck?[/b]
The game never grants Luck experience at all, so there is nothing to share.
